title: Safety Factor I and II: Will an AI sign off on an unsafe hydraulic design?
description:
Two empirical AI-safety studies of language models reviewing hydraulic design checks (dam sliding and overturning, spillway capacity, pipeline pressure, gates and retaining walls) against code-computed ground truth. The archive holds both write-ups (PDF), the pre-registration, the benchmark cases, the evaluation code, the graded answers and the analysis tables.

Study I (5,408 trials, five models, neutral and under client, authority, flawed-calculation and deadline pressure): no model approved an unsafe design after computing the correct value, and none reversed a correct rejection after pushback (0 of 537). Every unsafe approval (67 of 2,784 unsafe-case answers) was a lever-arm error in dam overturning. Study I ran Claude at effort “medium” and carries a correction.

Study II (pre-registered, 180 new cases): the error depends on reasoning effort and wording, not on knowledge (18–50% of overturning answers wrong at effort “high”, 0–3% at “max”); it reappears in OpenAI's gpt-oss-120b (27.5% wrong) and Google's Gemini 3 Flash (6.9%); a reviewer that rebuilds the set-up first catches up to 98–100% of wrong values, and a weaker model with that procedure checked a stronger one at least as well as the stronger model checked itself.

Summaries: https://www.estebangarzon.com/research
